text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israel ignores the world...begins construction on the Jebel Abu Ghneim settlement in occupied Jerusalem.
- One million acres of arable land in Toshka and work on the pumping station to begin in July.
- Early retirement scheme for public sector workers to cost state 11 billion pounds ($3.2 billion).

- Cabinet approves draft laws to encourage investment and change the sales tax. Another bill to increase rent five-fold and four-fold for shop tenants who are leasing space built in 1944 and 1961 and by 10 percent for those built between 1977 and 1996. Leases to increase by 10 percent annually.

- President Hosni Mubarak in an interview with the Israeli "Jerusalem Report" magazine: Egyptian-Israeli relations will remain cold for a long time. How can we normalise ties with Israel if they continue to kill our brothers?
- Youth entitled to a 10 year tax exemption on all projects.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the Jerusalem settlement will destroy the peace process and Israel must face the consequences. Contacts with Arab countries to face the dangers.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri to inaugurate the Cairo International Trade Fair today.
